title: Subcritical bifurcation and on-off bistability in ballistic polariton condensates
authors: Oleg I. Utesov, Soohong Choi, Pavel Kozhevin, Min Park, Daegwang Choi, Hyungdo Lee, Alexey N. Osipov, Alexey V. Yulin, Se Kwon Kim, Yong-Hoon Cho, Igor S. Aranson, Hyoungsoon Choi, Anton V. Nalitov, Sergei V. Koniakhin
abstract: Dynamics of exciton-polariton condensates under continuous-wave incoherent Gaussian optical pumping is considered. It is shown that the conventional supercritical Stuart-Landau picture is invalid in a certain domain of the parameter space. For strong polariton repulsion from the reservoir and relatively small pump spots, the dynamics is adequately described by the quintic Stuart-Landau equation. The corresponding subcritical pitchfork bifurcation leads to condensate formation, accompanied by bistability between the trivial and nontrivial states over a finite pump-power range and a one-bit memory. Further increase of the repulsion parameter or decrease of the spot size breaks down the perturbative approach and leads to a peculiar self-trapping regime with complex dynamics. Experimental evidence of the emergence of the proposed behavior is provided. Our findings can be used to design polaritonic setups that exploit the predicted memory effect.
summary: This paper analyzes the non-equilibrium dynamics of polariton condensates, finding that the standard theoretical model breaks down under certain conditions. It introduces the quintic Stuart-Landau equation to accurately describe the system, revealing the existence of subcritical bifurcation, which manifests as observable on-off bistability and memory effects. This has implications for designing polaritonic devices that exploit these memory properties.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamics of exciton-polariton condensates, demonstrating that the standard supercritical Stuart-Landau description fails in certain parameter regimes.
main_result: The system exhibits subcritical pitchfork bifurcation, leading to observable on-off bistability and a one-bit memory effect, which requires using a quintic Stuart-Landau equation for accurate modeling.
method: The study combines theoretical analysis (deriving and solving the quintic Stuart-Landau equation) with numerical simulations and comparison to experimental measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is an exciton-polariton condensate in a microcavity, modeled using a mean-field driven-dissipative Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The analysis simplifies this to the quintic Stuart-Landau equation near the condensation threshold.
key_observables: Bistability (hysteresis) between trivial and non-trivial condensate states, spectral line blueshift, and condensate intensity vs. pump power.
important_parameters: Pumping power, pump spot size ($r_0$), repulsion parameter ($g$), and the bifurcation parameter $c'$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on weak nonlinearity approximations, and the quintic equation is used to correct the standard Stuart-Landau model when the bifurcation is subcritical.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase flow showing bistability, the dependence of bifurcation parameters on pump spot size and repulsion, and simulated/experimental hysteresis loops for condensate intensity.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from the full governing equations (ddGPE) to deriving the applicable amplitude equations (cGLE, then quintic Stuart-Landau). It then analyzes the resulting subcritical bifurcation, discusses the self-trapping regime, and validates the theory using simulated and experimental measurements of intensity and spectral shifts.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for non-equilibrium phase transitions in interacting bosonic systems (polaritons), specifically identifying when and how the dynamics transition from simple supercritical behavior to complex, hysteretic subcritical regimes.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Sketch of the phase flow for the condensate ampli- tude |A0| according to Eqs. (9) and (13). In the conventional Stuart-Landau picture for the single-spot exciton-polariton condensate above the pumping threshold, there is a single stable fixed point that determines its density. For the subcrit- ical regime above the threshold, there is also a single stable fixed point. In contrast, slightly below the threshold, there are two stable fixed points: a non-trivial one with a nonzero condensate density and a trivial one with |A0| = 0, leading to bistability and memory effects. Upon further decrease of the pumping power, the nontrivial fixed point loses stability.

FIG. 3. For yet smaller pumping spots and stronger repul- sions from the reservoir, the ballistic condensate solution is subject to self-trapping. At the linear stage |A| ≪1, it grows following the pumping profile. When the condensate density is large enough, γ|A|2 ∼1, it “collapses” to a narrow spot, thus reducing the potential energy due to repulsion from the reservoir. The reservoir is essentially depleted in the center (so-called “hole-burning” effect). The self-trapped state is dy- namically unstable. Depending on the model parameters, it can blast as a circular wave (upper-right panel) or “tunnel” from the trap (bottom-right panel) in a random direction.
